source_text: Haec in utroque sexu positos inimicos nostros urtica commovit, quae olim quidem vitio malae consuetudinis mordax, tamen exhortationum salutarium velut quibusdam curabatur unguentis.
pass_a_gloss: This nettle has stirred our enemies placed in either sex, which formerly, to be sure, was biting by the vice of an evil custom, yet was treated by the ointments, as it were, of wholesome exhortations.

lemmas.lexica: LS malum; Blaise malum naturale vs malum voluntatis

pass_b_english: This nettle has stirred up our enemies of both sexes. Formerly its sting, produced by the vice of evil habit, was nevertheless treated with the ointments, so to speak, of wholesome exhortation.

choices.why: Julian's name for the doctrine he attacks: evil as a nature rather than as will.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
